CO actively continues exploring several areas of innovative finance for SDGs. The notable achievements are as follows: a. UNDP is currently implemented the Livelihood and Community Development project in Lubuk Bangkar, Jambi Province. The project is co-financed by the National Zakat Board of Republic Indonesia (BAZNAS) amounting to $80K. The project encompasses agriculture, micro-hydro power plant management, tourism, and MSMEs (youth and women empowerment). It is expected that the project will result in a self-sufficient economy by harnessing local commodities in diverse livelihood activities. In addition, a concept note for BAZNAS is being prepared together with Social Innovation Platform (SIP) and Biodiversity Finance Initiative (Biofin) projects. b. In addition to Islamic finance, CO has supported Indonesian Waqf Board and the Green Waqf Movement Team in the development of a green Waqf framework, which aims to utilize waqf to support climate actions in impoverished areas with tangible social-environmental impacts. The report was disseminated widely on the 21 September 2022 in collaboration with BWI. This report serves as a global reference on Islamic finance from Indonesia, which has demonstrated actions on advancing Islamic finance for sustainable development and addressing the climate crisis. It covers comprehensive information on Waqf and climate change initiatives, involving the government, private sector and grass-root communities c. CO has kicked off the implementation of Blue Finance Accelerator in August 2022, together with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the Indonesian Coordinating Ministry of Maritime and Investment Affairs. The Blue Finance Accelerator program aims to enhance the Government of Indonesia’s commitments and capacities for the Blue Economy and to leverage innovative financing instruments toward infrastructure programs supporting ocean preservation, community resilience, and the overall growth of the Blue Economy. d. The Blue Financing Strategic Document was launched by the Coordinating Minister of Maritime and Investment Affairs and UNDP on 12 October. The document aims to unravel the economic potential of marine-based economic activities and explore the capital market possibilities for investment in the blue economy. The document will become a reference for the government to issue blue bonds/sukuk in the coming years. e. Another achievement is CO’s support to the Ministry of Finance (MOF) in the development of the Insurance and Risk Finance Facility (IRFF). This document was launched in October and it lays the necessary groundwork for Indonesia to address multiple crisis such as changing climate, natural disasters, and the pandemic stalling development and exacerbating inequalities. f. The draft of the Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) Framework supported by UNDP CO currently is under review. The ESG framework will be implemented by the Ministry of Finance on the Public Private Partnership (PPP) infrastructure projects that received support from the government, both directly or through the Special Mission Vehicles (SMV) such as PT. SMI, PT. PII and PT. IIF. g. Role of private sector is immense – SDG Investor Map was successfully launched, and private equity Impact Fund has been developed in cooperation with the Indonesia Chamber of Commerce and a private fund management operator. h. The SDG Acceleration Diagnostic Tool has made progress, where the initial scoping has been completed with the finalisation of a Scoping Note. The Scoping note highlights Indonesia’s SDG Journey, mainstreaming to the National Medium term Development Plan (RPJMN), Institutional Arrangement and Policy, financing for SDG and findings, including gaps and priorities. CO will use Circular Economy as the lens to apply the accelerators in 2023.
